title: The Secret Garden
author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
level: Chinese junior-high (CEFR A2-B1). Simple English meanings.

disagreeable.meaning: Not nice. Unkind and not good to be with.

sour.meaning: Unhappy and cross. Here it shows in the look on a face.

ayah.meaning: In India, a woman whose job is to take care of a child.

sahib.meaning: In India, a word of respect. It is used for a European woman ('Mem Sahib') and for a girl ('Missie Sahib').

fretful.meaning: Unhappy, and crying or saying what is wrong all the time.

tyrannical.meaning: Using power over other people in a hard and unkind way.

governess.meaning: A woman who is paid to teach children at their home.

stammered.meaning: Spoke with many stops and the same sounds again and again, because of fear.

slunk.meaning: Moved quietly and secretly, because of fear or feeling bad about something done.

veranda.meaning: A covered place with a floor along the side of a house, open to the air.

hibiscus.meaning: A plant with a big, bright flower that grows in hot countries.

disdaining.meaning: Showing that you think something is not good enough for you.

imploringly.meaning: In a way that asks very hard for help.

wrung.meaning: Pressed hard and turned. 'Wrung her hands' shows great worry or sadness.

cholera.meaning: A very bad illness that spreads fast and can kill people.

bungalow.meaning: A house with only one floor, often in a hot country.

bewilderment.meaning: The state of not understanding and not knowing what to do.

hastily.meaning: Very quickly, because there is little time.

compound.meaning: The land with a wall around a group of buildings.

desolation.meaning: A sad, empty place where everyone has gone.

clergyman.meaning: A man whose job is to lead people in a church.

shabby.meaning: Old and worn, not looking good.

rockery.meaning: A part of a garden made with big stones and small plants.

contrary.meaning: Always going against what other people want.

hunchback.meaning: A person whose back is bent out into a round shape.

housekeeper.meaning: A person whose job is to run a big house and tell the other workers what to do.

mantle.meaning: A coat that does not fit close to the body, with no part for the arms, worn over other clothes.

fringe.meaning: An edge made of many small strings that fall from it.

bonnet.meaning: A covering for a woman's head, held on by a band that goes under the bottom of the face.

sallow.meaning: Of skin: a yellow colour that does not look healthy.

marred.meaning: Made worse. In this book a Yorkshire word for a child who has been brought up badly and gets cross over small things.

discomfited.meaning: Feeling uncomfortable and not sure what to do.

moor.meaning: A large area of high, open land with rough grass and no trees.

dreary.meaning: Sad and without anything nice to see or do.

lulled.meaning: Made quiet and ready to sleep by a soft, even sound.

stationmaster.meaning: The person in charge of a train station.

tha.meaning: A Yorkshire way to say 'you'. In the book it is often written tha'.

thee.meaning: A Yorkshire way to say 'you' (after a word like 'to'), used to one person.

thy.meaning: A Yorkshire and old way to say 'your'.

th.meaning: A short Yorkshire way to say 'the', written th' in the book.

aye.meaning: Yes. It is used in Yorkshire.

brougham.meaning: A closed vehicle pulled by a horse, used by rich people long ago.

footman.meaning: A man whose job is to open doors and help people get in and out of a vehicle.

coachman.meaning: A man whose job is to drive the horses that pull a vehicle.

cushioned.meaning: Made soft with something soft inside.

whitewashed.meaning: Made white by covering with a thin white liquid that is cheap.

vicarage.meaning: The house where the man who leads a village church lives.

heather.meaning: A low wild plant found on wild open hills. Its tiny flower is of a red-blue colour.

gorse.meaning: A wild plant with sharp points. Its flower is bright yellow.

broom.meaning: A wild plant with long thin branches. Its flower is yellow. Here it is a plant, not a tool for cleaning floors.

lodge.meaning: A small house at the way in to a big house or park.

vault.meaning: A curved top over a space. Here the trees make it look like the top of a long dark room.

ramble.meaning: To spread in all directions without order, as a big house does.

tapestry.meaning: A heavy cloth with a picture made in it, put up on a wall.

embroidered.meaning: Having a picture or design made on cloth with coloured string.

fantastically.meaning: In a very strange or surprising way.

turret.meaning: A small, thin, high part of a castle, built at a corner.

obsequious.meaning: Too ready to please a person who has power over you.

servile.meaning: Acting as if you have no wish of your own and doing all you are told.

salaam.meaning: In India, a way to show respect: bending low with the hand at the head.

scullery.meaning: A small room in a big house, used for cleaning the things used for cooking and eating.

indignantly.meaning: In an angry way, because something seems unfair.

humiliation.meaning: The feeling of being made to look silly in front of others.

subservient.meaning: Too ready to do what other people say.

totter.meaning: To walk with weak steps, as if you may fall.

homely.meaning: Simple, like home. Here it means friendly and kind, not grand.

treacle.meaning: A thick, sweet, dark liquid used on food.

victuals.meaning: Food. This is an old word.

marmalade.meaning: A sweet sticky food made from fruit, put on food in the morning.

ivy.meaning: A plant with dark green leaves that grows up walls.

crustily.meaning: In a rude and not friendly way.

meddlin.meaning: Taking part in things that are not your business. The book writes it as meddlin'.

wench.meaning: An old word for a girl or young woman.

forrad.meaning: A Yorkshire way to say 'forward'. Here it means too early.

blunt.meaning: Saying what you think in a direct way, without trying to be polite.

warrant.meaning: To say you are sure of something. 'I warrant' means 'I am sure'.

tapestried.meaning: Having walls covered with heavy cloth that has pictures made in it.

preen.meaning: When a bird preens, it cleans and puts in order the soft covering of its body with its beak.

wutherin.meaning: A Yorkshire word for the sound of strong wind, a loud low noise that goes on and on. The book writes it as wutherin'.

buffeting.meaning: Hitting something again and again, as the wind does.

shuddering.meaning: Moving the body in short quick movements because of fear or cold.

moithered.meaning: A Yorkshire word for mixed up and upset by too much noise or work, not able to think clearly.

collie.meaning: A kind of dog with long hair, used on a farm to watch the animals.

perplexed.meaning: Not understanding and not sure what to do or think.

pewter.meaning: A soft metal used to make cups and bowls.

romping.meaning: Playing in a loud, rough way.

gallery.meaning: A long room or hall, here with pictures on the walls.

ruffs.meaning: Wide, round neck-cloths with many bends in them, worn long ago.

brocade.meaning: A rich cloth with a raised design in it.

inlaid.meaning: With small pieces of another material set into the surface to make a picture.

mantel.meaning: The part above a fire in the wall of a room, where you can put things.

cabinet.meaning: A tall box with doors, for keeping things.

ivory.meaning: The hard white material from the long teeth of a very large animal with a long nose.

mahout.meaning: A man in India whose job is to ride and look after a very large animal with a long nose.

palanquin.meaning: A covered seat or bed carried by people on long sticks, or on an animal.

dialect.meaning: A way of speaking that is special to one part of a country.

soart.meaning: A Yorkshire way to say 'sort', meaning 'kind'.

vixon.meaning: The way a Yorkshire speaker says a word for a sharp, angry girl or woman. The mother of Martha uses it for a cross girl.

daffydowndilly.meaning: An old, playful name for a yellow flower that comes in spring.

mole.meaning: A small animal that makes long holes in the ground to live in.

howsoever.meaning: However. This is an old way to say it.

contrariness.meaning: Going against what other people want, again and again.

fumbling.meaning: Using your hands badly to find or hold something.

skip.meaning: To jump over a rope that is turned under your feet and over your head.

tuppence.meaning: A small amount of old British money, worth two of the smallest pieces.

impudence.meaning: Rude words or actions that show no respect.

clumsy.meaning: Not smooth or careful in how you move; likely to drop things or hit them.

trill.meaning: A quick, high song of a bird, with the same sound again and again, fast.

knob.meaning: A round handle on a door.

heathen.meaning: A person who does not follow the religion of the speaker. Here it is said of people who do not follow his own faith.

pipin.meaning: Very hot. The book writes it as pipin'.

tendril.meaning: A thin part of a plant that goes round things and holds on.

hazy.meaning: Not clear, as if seen through thin smoke.

alcove.meaning: A small space set back in a wall or in a line of plants.

urn.meaning: A tall container with a wide top and a base, used for plants.

bulb.meaning: A round part of a plant under the ground, from which a flower grows.

narcissus.meaning: A white or yellow flower of spring, often grown in gardens.

jonquil.meaning: A small yellow or white flower that comes in spring.

eyeteeth.meaning: The two pointed teeth at the top of the mouth, on each side of the front teeth. 'Like pulling eyeteeth' means very hard to do.

dictated.meaning: Spoke words for someone else to write down.

restlessly.meaning: In a way that shows you cannot keep still.

flightiness.meaning: Acting in a way that changes quickly and cannot be trusted.

hobnailed.meaning: Of shoes: with thick pieces of metal in the bottom to make them strong.

danged.meaning: A mild way to say 'damned', used by Ben in the book to show surprise.

bachelder.meaning: A man who is not married, as a Yorkshire speaker says it.

rheumatics.meaning: An old word for a sickness that makes the knees and other joints hurt.

pheasant.meaning: A large wild bird with a long tail. People shoot it for food.

tremulous.meaning: Not firm; moving a little in a way you cannot stop.

trowel.meaning: A small garden tool with a short handle, used to make small holes in the ground.

hoe.meaning: A garden tool with a long handle and a flat end, used for cutting down unwanted plants.

larkspur.meaning: A tall garden plant. Its flower is blue or white.

mignonette.meaning: A small garden plant with a flower that is sweet to the nose.

flout.meaning: To show that you do not respect someone, in an open way.

sidled.meaning: Moved to one side, in small quick steps, as a bird does.

obstinate.meaning: Not willing to change your mind, even when other people ask you to.

defiantly.meaning: In a way that shows you will not do as you are told.

creeper.meaning: A plant that grows up walls or trees.

lichen.meaning: A flat growth of light green colour that covers trees and stones.

upholding.meaning: Holding up; carrying the weight of something.

wick.meaning: A Yorkshire word for alive and full of life. In the book Mary is told that it means alive or lively.

nesh.meaning: A Yorkshire word for weak or easily hurt by cold.

whitethorn.meaning: A small tree with sharp points. Its flower is white.

knobstick.meaning: A stick with a round end at the top.

spick.meaning: Used with one more word to mean very clean and in good order.

distended.meaning: Made bigger and full to the edge, because it has too much inside.

lily.meaning: A tall garden plant with a large, beautiful flower.

missel.meaning: Part of the name of a big brown bird that sings.

brooch.meaning: A small shiny thing worn on clothes for show.

quavered.meaning: Spoke with a voice that was not strong and even.

faltered.meaning: Spoke in a weak, unsure way.

tiresome.meaning: Making you feel tired or cross.

ajar.meaning: A little open. A door that is ajar is not fully closed.

rebellious.meaning: Not willing to do what rules or people in charge say.

agate.meaning: A hard stone with lines of colour. The book uses it for the colour of Colin's eyes.

wrapper.meaning: A piece of clothing worn over night clothes.

invalid.meaning: A person who is ill or weak for a long time.

clambered.meaning: Went up in a rough way, using hands and feet.

tramp.meaning: To walk with heavy steps through a place.

tantrum.meaning: A sudden fit of anger, like a child's.

bewitched.meaning: Changed by what seems like magic.

sylum.meaning: Short for an old word for a place where people who are very ill in the mind are kept.

raved.meaning: Spoke wildly, as if out of his mind.

brace.meaning: A hard support worn on the body to hold the back straight.

rheumatic.meaning: Having a sickness that makes the knees and other joints hurt.

typhoid.meaning: A serious sickness that makes the body very hot.

brocaded.meaning: Made of rich cloth with a raised design.

curtsy.meaning: A way a girl or woman shows respect: bending the knees with one foot back.

charm.meaning: To make animals or people do as you wish, as if by magic.

burrows.meaning: Holes in the ground made by animals to live in.

sly.meaning: Clever in a quiet way, in order to find out things or get what you want.

slamp.meaning: A Yorkshire word meaning to lie down flat. It is said of hair that will not lie flat on the head.

nigh.meaning: A Yorkshire and old word for near. 'Not nigh so' means 'not nearly so'.

waft.meaning: A light movement of air carrying something that your nose picks up.

fluting.meaning: Making soft, high, sweet sounds, as a singing bird does.

scores.meaning: Many; 20 or more. 'Scores of birds' means very many birds.

unbolt.meaning: To open a door by pulling back the metal bar that holds it shut.

herbaceous.meaning: Of plants whose parts above the ground die each winter and grow again. 'Herbaceous beds' are garden beds of such plants.

unfurling.meaning: Opening out from a rolled-up shape.

plumaged.meaning: Having a certain kind of soft covering on a bird's body. In the book it is shiny.

alighted.meaning: Came down and landed, as a bird does.

tousled.meaning: With hair that is not in order.

rook.meaning: A big black bird that lives in groups in tall trees.

munnot.meaning: A Yorkshire way to say 'must not'.

meddle.meaning: To get into something that is not your business.

cripple.meaning: An old word for a person who cannot walk or move well. Here it means someone whose body does not grow straight.

gauze.meaning: Very thin, light cloth that you can see through.

veil.meaning: A thin cloth that covers the face or something else.

condescended.meaning: Did something kind as if you were too good for the person.

nutcracker.meaning: A tool with two arms, used to break open hard shells. In the book a face is said to look like one, sharp and thin.

vixen.meaning: A female wild animal like a small dog with a red coat. Used for a girl who is sharp and angry.

hysterics.meaning: Wild crying and screaming that a person cannot control.

monogram.meaning: Letters of a person's name put together in a design on something.

pampered.meaning: Given too much care, and everything you want.

restrain.meaning: To hold someone back from doing something.

writhe.meaning: To turn the body about, as if in pain.

hunch.meaning: A round part of the back that sticks out, on a person with a bent back.

graidely.meaning: A Yorkshire word for fine, great or very good.

chap.meaning: A man or boy. Here it is used in a friendly way.

affectation.meaning: Acting in a way that is not natural, to seem nicer or better than you are.

enraptured.meaning: Filled with great happiness and wonder.

wands.meaning: Thin sticks used in stories to do magic.

spires.meaning: Tall, thin points. Here, tall narrow shapes made by one kind of flower.

unscrupulous.meaning: Willing to do wrong things to get what you want.

bromide.meaning: A medicine that makes a person quiet and ready to sleep.

volubly.meaning: In a way that uses many words, talking easily.

shrewd.meaning: Clever about people and money; having good sense.

recluse.meaning: A person who lives alone and keeps away from other people.

austerely.meaning: In a serious, cold way, with no softness.

ravenous.meaning: Very hungry. Here it is said of how a very young animal drinks milk.

bleat.meaning: A thin cry, as made by a farm animal with a thick white coat.

columbine.meaning: A garden flower with small curved parts that look like tails.

snapdragon.meaning: A garden flower that opens and shuts like a mouth when you press it.

signet.meaning: A ring with a small picture or letters cut into it, used by important people to make their sign on letters.

salaams.meaning: Ways of showing respect in India: bending low with the hand at the head.

sulky.meaning: Quiet and cross because you are not pleased.

primrose.meaning: A small light yellow flower of spring.

transported.meaning: Carried from one place to another.

rumors.meaning: Stories that people tell, without knowing if they are true.

uncanny.meaning: Strange, in a way that makes you a little afraid.

humped.meaning: With a round part sticking out on the back.

menagerie.meaning: A collection of wild animals kept together.

servitor.meaning: An old word for a person who does work for another and does what he is told.

morbid.meaning: Having dark, sad thoughts, especially about sickness and death.

garlands.meaning: Rings of leaves and flower, worn or put up for show.

procession.meaning: A long line of people moving along together.

tendrils.meaning: Thin parts of a plant that go round things and hold on.

fanciful.meaning: Made up in the mind, not real.

consort.meaning: The husband or wife of a king or queen. 'Prince Consort' was the title of Queen Victoria's husband.

canopy.meaning: A cover that spreads over a place high up.

flusters.meaning: Makes someone feel worried and not able to think clearly.

rhododendron.meaning: A big garden plant that is full of large, bright flower in spring.

crumpets.meaning: Small round soft food eaten hot with butter.

lances.meaning: Long thin spears. Here it means long thin lines of light from the sun.

harangued.meaning: Spoke angrily and for a long time.

besom.meaning: A Yorkshire word for a cross woman or girl who makes trouble. It is also the word for a tool for cleaning floors.

drat.meaning: An old word used when you are cross.

impidint.meaning: A Yorkshire way to say a word that means rude and showing no respect.

imperiously.meaning: In a proud way that expects people to do as told.

gnarled.meaning: Rough and bent out of shape, like very old wood.

tactless.meaning: Saying things without thinking how they may hurt.

disentangle.meaning: To free from something that holds it.

gabbled.meaning: Spoke very fast and not clearly.

lath.meaning: A thin, narrow piece of wood.

abide.meaning: To bear or put up with someone.

majesty.meaning: Great beauty and power that make people feel respect.

reigned.meaning: Ruled, as a king does. Here it means happiness was everywhere.

jackasses.meaning: Male animals like small horses; the name is used for silly people.

brayin.meaning: Making the loud, rough cry of an animal like a small horse. The book writes it as brayin'.

pluck.meaning: Being brave when things are hard.

exultation.meaning: Very great happiness because you have won.

persevered.meaning: Kept trying and did not give up.

hobbled.meaning: Walked slowly in an uneven way, with trouble.

overexert.meaning: To work your body too hard.

slapping.meaning: Hitting with the open hand. 'A slapping sort of man' means a man who hits people.

prejudice.meaning: A bad opinion formed before you know the facts. 'Without prejudice' means with a fair mind.

crevices.meaning: Narrow openings in a wall or rock.

satiny.meaning: Smooth and shiny, like a soft cloth.

sundial.meaning: A tool in a garden that shows the time by where the sun makes a dark line.

unsheath.meaning: To take out of a cover. Here it means new growth opening out of its covers.

acquaintance.meaning: Knowledge of a person or thing. 'Make the acquaintance of' means get to know.

fakirs.meaning: Holy men in India who live very simply and are said to do wonderful things.

imposing.meaning: Making people feel respect because it seems great.

orator.meaning: A person who makes a speech.

devotees.meaning: People who give themselves fully to a religion or to something they love.

majestic.meaning: Grand and beautiful, like a king.

dervishes.meaning: Holy men who move round and round as part of their religion.

athlete.meaning: A person who is very good at sports and is strong.

prizefighter.meaning: A man who fights with his hands for money.

experiment.meaning: A test that you make to find out if something is true.

scientific.meaning: Of science; done in a careful way to find out facts.

fascination.meaning: A strong power to hold your interest.

twilight.meaning: The soft, low light after the sun has gone down.

haze.meaning: Thin smoke or water in the air that makes things hard to see clearly.

pother.meaning: A state of worry and noise about small things.

currants.meaning: Small dried black fruit, used in sweet food.

bloated.meaning: Made too big and full, with air or water.

clotted.meaning: Thick and heavy. Here it is said of a very thick yellow food made from milk.

pantry.meaning: A small room where food is kept.

mystic.meaning: Having a secret or holy meaning.

tinge.meaning: A small amount of a colour.

wrestler.meaning: A person who fights by holding and throwing the other person.

muscle.meaning: A part of the body that lets you move and be strong.

revelation.meaning: The telling of something that was not known.

riot.meaning: Wild and loud action. Here, wild, happy feeling.

nourishment.meaning: Food that keeps a body healthy and growing.

fowl.meaning: A bird such as a chicken, used for food.

gibberish.meaning: Talk that has no meaning, or that someone cannot understand.

secrete.meaning: To keep out of sight. Here, a small bird puts itself out of sight among a plant's leaves.

disconcerting.meaning: Making you feel uneasy and not sure what to do.

fledged.meaning: Grown up enough to fly (of a young bird).

brooded.meaning: Sat over, as a bird sits over eggs to keep them warm. Here, 'brooded over by a great peace' means filled with peace.

restive.meaning: Not able to keep still; restless.

inordinately.meaning: Much more than is right or normal.

pilgrimage.meaning: A trip to a special place. Here, Mary's first walk through the empty rooms.

parrot.meaning: A bird with bright colours that can copy words.

incantations.meaning: Words said again and again, as if to make magic.

devouring.meaning: Looking hungrily, as if wanting to take in everything.

doxology.meaning: A short song that thanks God, used in church.

dappling.meaning: Making spots of light and dark.

gloating.meaning: Looking with great happiness, often in a proud way.

tremulously.meaning: In a way that is not firm, with the voice or body moving a little.

bandy.meaning: Bent out at the knees, with the legs wide apart.

wilt.meaning: An old form of 'will' used when speaking to one person as 'you'.

drumsticks.meaning: Sticks used to make music by hitting; here, thin legs.

hypochondriac.meaning: A person who is always afraid that he is ill, even when he is not.

thistle.meaning: A wild plant with sharp points on its leaves and a red-blue flower.

fjords.meaning: Long, narrow arms of the sea between high hills of rock, in Norway.

gentians.meaning: Deep blue flower of the mountains.

stagnant.meaning: Not moving or flowing, so that it goes bad. Said of water.

salver.meaning: A flat piece of metal for carrying letters or food on.

sovereign.meaning: An old British piece of money made of gold.

embowered.meaning: Shut in by branches of trees, like a room.

scuffling.meaning: Making the sound of feet moving about in a rough way.

stepladder.meaning: A short set of steps to stand on, which stands by itself.

villa.meaning: A large house in the country, often in a warm place.

sup.meaning: To drink a little at a time.

germ.meaning: A very small living thing that can cause disease.

queer.whyHard: It is not a rude name for a person. Here it means strange.

mistress.meaning: An old title for a girl or a woman, like Miss.

servant.meaning: A person whose job is to work in a house.

creature.meaning: A living animal, or a person thought of as a living thing.

native.meaning: A person born in that country. Here, the servants from India.

cottage.meaning: A small house in the country.

corridor.meaning: A long passage inside a house, with rooms along it.

manor.meaning: A large old house with land around it.

nest.meaning: The home a bird makes for its eggs.

branch.meaning: A part of a tree that grows out from the stem.

cheek.meaning: The soft part of the face beside the mouth.

forehead.meaning: The part of the face above the eyes.

fox.meaning: A wild animal with a pointed face, pointed ears, and a thick tail.

robin.meaning: A small bird with a bright red front.

squirrel.meaning: A small animal with a big bushy tail that lives in trees.

skylark.meaning: A small bird that sings high in the sky.

cub.meaning: A young fox or other young wild animal.

beak.meaning: The hard mouth of a bird.

carriage.meaning: A closed seat on wheels that horses pull.

spade.meaning: A tool with a long handle and a flat blade, for digging.

hearth.meaning: The stone floor of a fireplace, where the fire is.

hearthrug.meaning: A small rug laid in front of the fireplace.

grate.meaning: The metal bars that hold a fire in a fireplace.

nursery.meaning: A room where a young child sleeps and plays.

orchard.meaning: A piece of ground where fruit trees grow.

fountain.meaning: A place where water shoots up and falls back into a pool.

velvet.meaning: A soft thick cloth that feels smooth when you touch it.

curtain.meaning: A cloth hung over a window or an opening.

cushion.meaning: A soft bag to sit on or to lean against.

pillow.meaning: A soft bag for your head when you are in bed.

passage.meaning: A long narrow way inside a house.

shrubbery.meaning: A group of bushes planted together.

moorland.meaning: The open wild land of a moor.

lawn.meaning: Short grass that is cut and kept neat.

oak.meaning: A large tree with hard wood and a broad top.

ladder.meaning: A movable set of steps, used for climbing.

stool.meaning: A seat with no back or arms.

footstool.meaning: A low stool to rest your feet on.

rug.meaning: A small thick cover for the floor.

carpet.meaning: A thick cloth cover for a floor.

cloak.meaning: A loose outer coat with no sleeves.

apron.meaning: A cloth tied over your clothes to keep them clean.

waistcoat.meaning: A short sleeveless coat worn under a jacket.

stocking.meaning: A close-fitting cover for the foot and the lower leg.

handkerchief.meaning: A small cloth for the nose or the face.

porridge.meaning: Hot food made by boiling grain in water or milk.

shilling.meaning: An old British coin. Twelve pennies made one of them.

candle.meaning: A stick of wax with a string in it, burned to give light.

toast.meaning: Bread heated until it is brown.

bacon.meaning: Salted meat from the side of a pig.

ham.meaning: Meat from the leg of a pig.

wine.meaning: A strong drink made from grapes.

cart.meaning: A simple wagon, often pulled by a horse.

stable.meaning: A building where horses are kept.

cockle.meaning: A small sea animal with two shells.

poppy.meaning: A flower with thin petals, often red.

bud.meaning: A small closed part of a plant that will open into a leaf or a flower.

blossom.meaning: A flower, especially on a tree.

weed.meaning: A wild plant growing where you do not want it.

pipe.meaning: A small tube you blow to make a simple tune.

spray.meaning: A long thin stem with leaves or flowers on it.

flowerbed.meaning: A piece of ground where flowers are planted.

treetop.meaning: The highest part of a tree.

lump.meaning: A small round part that sticks out or sticks together.

mate.meaning: The partner a bird or animal pairs with.

feather.meaning: One of the light pieces that cover a bird.

bough.meaning: A large branch of a tree.

lap.meaning: The flat top of your legs when you sit.

throat.meaning: The front of the neck, and the passage inside it.

flesh.meaning: The soft part of the body.

spine.meaning: The row of bones down the back.

fork.meaning: A tool with points. A small one is for eating, and a big one is for digging.

package.meaning: A wrap of paper or a small parcel of things.

clump.meaning: A group of plants growing close together.

evergreen.meaning: A plant that stays green all winter.

cabbage.meaning: A round green vegetable with thick leaves.

mist.meaning: A thin cloud close to the ground.

custom.meaning: The usual way something is done.

duty.meaning: The thing a person ought to do.

curiosity.meaning: A wish to know about something.

scent.meaning: A smell, often a pleasant one.

manner.meaning: The way a person behaves or speaks.

expression.meaning: The look on a person's face.

speech.meaning: The way someone talks, or the words they say.

fashion.meaning: A way of doing or saying something.
